turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
The README already points to `internal/mapengine/`. Let me look at its structure and the routing logic in detail.This confirms the exact selection logic. Now let me check where `Map` is called from (the CLI/read command) and verify the treesitter language table for completeness.Good — confirms `internal/ghx/read.go` is the call site. Let me check that plus the CLI flag wiring in `internal/cli/ghx.go`.Good, that confirms the wiring. Let me get the CLI flag definitions too.I have everything needed to answer. This all comes directly from reading the actual source in the repo via `ghx`, no cloning involved.

## Structural map engine

**Package:** `internal/mapengine/` (Go, ~24KB across 5 files)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `types.go` | Shared types (`Engine`, `Level`, `Kind`, `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`, `Mapper` interface) and the **dispatch logic**: `Map()`, `mapAuto()`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback()`, `buildResultFromSymbols()` |
| `goast.go` | `GoASTMapper` — parses Go via stdlib `go/ast` + `go/parser`/`go/token` |
| `treesitter.go` | `TreeSitterMapper` — uses [gotreesitter](https://github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter) grammars/tagger for TS/JS/Python/Rust |
| `regex.go` | `RegexMapper` — line-pattern fallback (`regexRules` map keyed by extension) for everything else |
| `regex_test.go` | Tests for the regex mapper |

Confirmed by `ghx read --map` output showing exactly these function signatures in each file (`internal/mapengine/types.go:125` `func Map(...)`, `:143` `func mapAuto(...)`, etc.) and by ADR `docs/adr/0013-ghx-map-command.md`, which states: *"`internal/mapengine` owns `Mapper`, `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`, engine selection, fallback, and output formatting."*

## Engine selection per file

Selection happens in `mapAuto()` at `internal/mapengine/types.go:143-157`, keyed on `filepath.Ext(path)`:

```go
func mapAuto(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".go":
		result, err := GoASTMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
		if err == nil { return result, nil }
		fallback, _ := RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)   // Go parse error → regex fallback
		fallback.Fallback = true
		return fallback, nil
	case ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".py", ".rs":
		return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(path, content, opts, false)
	default:
		return RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
	}
}
```

- **`.go`** → `GoASTMapper` (stdlib `go/ast`), falls back to regex on a parse error.
- **`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx`/`.py`/`.rs`** → `TreeSitterMapper` via `mapTreeSitterWithFallback()` (`types.go:160`), which tries tree-sitter first and falls back to `RegexMapper` on `ErrUnsupportedLanguage` or any other error.
- **Everything else** → `RegexMapper` directly.

This is the `auto` case of the outer `Map()` dispatcher (`types.go:125-141`), which also supports forcing an engine explicitly:
```go
switch opts.Engine {
case EngineRegex:      return RegexMapper{}.Map(...)
case EngineTreeSitter: return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., true)
case EngineAuto:       return mapAuto(...)
default:               /* unknown engine string → regex fallback with warning */
}
```

**Call chain to the CLI:**
- `internal/ghx/read.go:187-196` calls `mapengine.Map(path, content, mapengine.Options{Engine: opts.MapEngine, Level: ..., Kind: ...})` when `opts.Map` is true, and stores `result.MapEngine` in the read result for reporting.
- `internal/cli/ghx.go:112,211` defines the `--map-engine` flag (default `"auto"`) on the `read` command and passes it through as `ReadOpts.MapEngine` — so `auto` is the default and only overridden if the user passes `--map-engine regex|tree-sitter`.
- The MCP server (`internal/cli/serve.go`) exposes the same choice as a `mapEngine` string parameter (`auto|regex|tree-sitter`).

### Not verified
- I did not read the full body of `treesitter.go`'s `languageConfigs()`/`defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs()` (lines 121-333) in detail, so I can't confirm exact per-language tag-query differences (e.g. Python's custom signature formatting) beyond the function names seen in the map.
- I did not inspect the `gotreesitter` dependency itself (external repo) — its grammar/tagging internals are out of scope and unverified here.
- I did not run the binary; all conclusions are from static reading of source via `ghx read`/`search`, not execution.

README:
# ghx — the code-reconnaissance sidecar for AI agents

**Expensive main agents shouldn't burn frontier tokens on tree/grep/read loops.**
ghx is a cheap, specialized **sidecar agent** that a main agent delegates code
reconnaissance to. Ask it a repo question in plain English; it explores GitHub
under the hood and hands back a **schema-validated evidence report** — claims
with citations, the commands it ran, and what it could not confirm — while every
artifact of the investigation lands on disk under `~/.ghx/sessions/` for you or
the parent agent to inspect.

This is the first public cut of the **Agent Sidecar Framework**: a main agent
delegates a whole competence domain to a proficient specialist instead of loading
that domain's tools and doctrine into its own context. ghx is the proof — the
code-reconnaissance sidecar — and, underneath it, a sharp standalone GitHub
exploration CLI. The durable vision lives in
[docs/NORTH_STAR.md](docs/NORTH_STAR.md).

> ghx is two products in one binary: a **sidecar brain** you delegate to (this
> README's lead), and the **classic exploration CLI** it drives under the hood
> (documented in full further down). Use whichever fits; they share one core.

## Why a sidecar

When a main agent stops mid-task to explore code, the real cost is not the API

the thread of the engineering work, and the ~400 lines of tool doctrine it needs
